title: Session horizon retention and forensic reporting playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: Define an implementable playbook for 'session horizon' retention semantics across prompts, responses, request logs, embeddings, and derived metrics, plus automated forensic/evidence export paths. Goal: give customers predictable, region-aware defaults and per-route overrides, provide clear legal-hold semantics, and ship console UX + API hooks for exporting tamper-evident evidence bundles.
acceptance_criteria: Spec includes concrete TTL modes: fixed TTL, sliding session horizon, sticky retention for flagged sessions
Retention applies per-tenant, per-route, and per-session with residency-aware enforcement
Console UI mocks and API fields documented for setting retention mode and retention TTL per route
Evidence export format defined (signed manifest, compressed artifacts, SHA256 checksums, KMS envelope) and sample export automation works end-to-end in staging
Legal-hold flag prevents deletion for specified session IDs and appears in audit log with reason and TTL override
Rollout plan with telemetry and regression checks to monitor cost and storage growth
Security review completed and integration test added to CI for purge behavior
tasks: Draft engineering PRD with retention modes and enforcement model
Design console controls and evidence export modal
Agree on evidence bundle schema with Security/Legal
Prototype export job that collects logs, prompts, embeddings and signs bundle
Implement per-route retention API and backend eviction scheduler
Add audit timeline entries for retention changes and legal holds
Create QA plan and e2e test harness in staging
Prepare rollout checkpoints and cost guardrails

2026-03-09 Security review: small feedback to include key rotation ID in bundle metadata and to sign using HSM-backed KMS where available.

decisions: Initial scope: implement fixed TTL and sliding session horizon; postpone sticky retention per-customer feature to Q3
Evidence bundle schema will be TAR+GZIP with a JSON manifest containing SHA256 checksums and KMS envelope metadata
Console will expose per-route retention controls and a one-click evidence export modal; heavy exports will run as async jobs
Legal hold will be an explicit boolean with optional reason and owner fields surfaced in audit logs
